# Emergency recovery

Things that go wrong mid-session, and what to do about each. The general rule: the capture log
is append-only and hash-chained, so the recovery is almost always to add a record rather than
to edit one. Editing history breaks the chain and the gate will say so.

## The laptop died mid-capture

Nothing is lost. The log is appended one line at a time and fsync'd, so at worst the final
line is torn. The next run detects that, moves the torn bytes to `manifest.jsonl.torn`, and
continues. Re-take the frame that was in flight; the app's NEXT ACTION will already be
pointing at it.

## A photograph is on the phone but not on the Mac

Re-transfer and add it again. Ingestion is content-addressed and idempotent: an identical file
already present is recognised and not duplicated, and an interrupted copy is either completed
or discovered to be complete.

## I deleted a photograph by accident

The gate will block on `captures.files_intact` and name the file. Restore it from the phone
(the hash in the manifest tells you whether you restored the right one), or re-take the frame.
A manifest entry whose file is gone is not evidence.

## The rig moved / the camera got knocked

Re-freeze it: `tools/pilot.py setup <GARMENT> --reason "..."`. This mints a NEW setup hash and
records the change. Captures taken under the old hash stay valid and stay labelled with it;
nothing is retroactively re-attributed. If the change was large enough to matter, re-take the
frames that depended on it.

## The board got bent, reprinted, or replaced

Re-measure the squares and record the reading. If the new print is out of tolerance, the gate
blocks and it is right to: every scale derived from it would carry the error.

## I answered an intake question wrongly

Answer it again. Feature answers are appended, and the latest wins. If the correction ADDS a
feature, the plan grows and the new frames appear in NEXT ACTION. If it removes one, the
frames you already took stay in the log and are simply no longer required.

## The app says the log does not verify

Three different sentences, and they mean different things. A TORN FINAL LINE is an interrupted
append: the next run quarantines it into manifest.jsonl.torn and continues, and you re-take
the frame that was in flight. A CHAIN BREAK or MISMATCH means an entry was edited, inserted,
removed or reordered after it was written -- do not cut, and recover from the phone's own
copies. ENTRIES MISSING means the log is shorter than the anchor beside it says it once was:
something removed entries from the end.

None of these can be repaired by editing the log, and trying makes it worse: the chain is
recomputed from the file's own contents, so an edit that fixes one entry breaks every entry
after it. The recoverable path is always the same -- the photographs are still on the phone,
and re-ingesting them into a fresh session rebuilds a log that verifies.

## The app refuses a photograph that looks fine to me

Read which check refused it, because the four outcomes want different things. RETAKE means
something was measured and did not meet the requirement -- the message names it. UNAVAILABLE
means the check could not run at all: no board in frame, no scale, no earlier image to compare
against. That is not a fault in the photograph, and re-shooting the same frame will not clear
it; supply what is missing. HUMAN CHECK means no measurement can settle it and the app is
asking you to look.

## The gate says READY and I do not believe it

Run `tools/pilot.py precut <GARMENT> --json /tmp/v.json` and read the satisfied list. Every
condition names the evidence it accepted. If a condition passed that should not have, that is
a defect in the gate and it is more important than the garment: stop, and add the case to
`tools/pilot.py selftest`.

## I cut the garment and something was missing

Record it as a deviation immediately, while you remember it. The offcuts carry a raw edge
identical to the garment's, so some measurements can still be recovered from them. What cannot
be recovered is a before-state photograph, which is the whole reason the gate exists.
